title: Sway: Award-winning British rapper dies aged 44
description: Sway was born Derek Andrew Safo in London, albeit accidentally, while his mother was on a stop-over between Amsterdam and her native Ghana. After a br
body: Sway was born Derek Andrew Safo in London, albeit accidentally, while his mother was on a stop-over between Amsterdam and her native Ghana. After a brief period in her homeland, he was raised in north London and honed his craft on pirate radio. He credited the BBC's radio station 1Xtra with providing him with his first break in 2002.Emerging during the first wave of grime, alongside artists such as Dizzee Rascal and Lethal Bizzle, he stood apart for his witty, literate style."I'm a positive person. The positivity comes out in my music," he told the Guardian as his career took off. "I don't go round holding guns to people's heads so I won't rap about holding guns to people's heads."Despite widespread interest from the music industry, he remained independent - releasing music on his own label, and selling mixtapes at markets and independent record shops.He made headlines in September 2005 when he was named best hip-hop act at the Mobo awards - defeating US heavyweights such as 50 Cent and the Game.But in 2010, DaSafo was diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma. "It felt like I had been dropped in the middle of the sea with no lifejacket," he later recalled. "I didn't have time to think about how I was going to get to the other side, I just had to deal with it."After receiving chemotherapy and radiotherapy, he went into remission, releasing his biggest hits Still Speedin' (which sampled Black Box's Ride On Time) and Level Up (featuring a verse from Kano) in 2012.He enjoyed further critical and commercial success with albums including Deliverance, and Verses from the Vault; and collaborated with artists like Mark Ronson, Ed Sheeran, Akon and Childish Gambino.Through his record label Dcypha, he also signed and developed artists including Tiggs Da Author and KSI. All three appeared on the 2013 single No Sleep, and KSI went on to become a hugely successful YouTuber, with a sideline in music.DaSafo also dabbled with an acting career, appearing in two episodes of the crime drama Top Boy and the 2012 film The Grind.At the time of his death, he was working on new music. His final Instagram post, shared last week, external, celebrated his 44th birthday.He is survived by two sons, Jalil and Ammar-Joseph, and twin daughters, Queen-Inaya and Queen-Imara. At the time of his death, he was raising them as a single parent in Ghana, his friend Kash Ahmad told BBC News."It was an honour and a pleasure to have known and worked with him, and my thoughts and prayers are with his family," he added.Other tributes came from the Mitchell Brothers, who wrote: "We were privileged to have worked with you", and praised Sway's "true penmanship level and delivery"."This hit me like a ton of bricks," said rapper and record label executive Kardinal Offishall. "Rest in eternal peace and God cover your babies. Til we meet again my friend."So Solid Crew's Megaman simply posted "RIP"; while The Mobo Awards said they were "proud to have him as part of our history," adding: "Our love goes out to his family, loved ones and fans."Singer Lemar said: "Your talent knew no bounds. Blessed to have shared the stage with you."Rapper Baby Blue posted on Instagram: "In my heart I worried this day was coming but I wasn't prepared for the reality of losing Sway. "He was my confidante and he guided me through so much of my life musically and personally... I will miss you forever my friend. I am lost."Breaking the news to her listeners on BBC Radio 1Xtra, broadcaster Remi Burgz said it was a "sad day for British music" and called Sway a "UK Rap pioneer"."One of north London's finest," she said, "he was mine and many others first experience of UK rap [and] hip-hop in mainstream media"."He was a literal example of paving the way and showing that UK rap can take up space in music."Rest in perfect peace to Sway."

schema.headline: Sway: Award-winning British rapper dies aged 44

title: Badenoch brings in lawyers after 94% Wandsworth Council tax hike
description: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has said she has brought in lawyers to potentially challenge the government over local funding cuts, after a record
body: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has said she has brought in lawyers to potentially challenge the government over local funding cuts, after a record council tax rise in one of her party's flagship local authorities.She told BBC Newsnight the proposed 94% hike in Wandsworth, a south-west London borough run by the Tories, was "outrageous" but that "they're not doing it because they want to".Badenoch said the Conservative Party had "instructed lawyers" to see if an £84m-a-year government funding cut, which Wandsworth Council has blamed for the increase, can be blocked.The government said it was "fixing an outdated funding system so funding goes where need is greatest".Wandsworth has long had one of the lowest council tax rates in the country, with an average Band D property currently paying just over £1,000, compared to above £2,000 in an increasing number of London boroughs.But this would nearly double with the planned £958 rise.There has been heavy criticism since the move was announced in a council meeting on Tuesday. A final decision is to be made early next year.Changes to the funding formula for councils announced last year will see money redistributed from some council areas to others. Wandsworth Council said it stood to lose £84m annually in funding by the end of the next three years.Commenting for the first time on the row, Badenoch accused ministers of seemingly "taking money from areas that don't vote Labour and giving it to places that do vote Labour"."I think it is outrageous that Wandsworth Council is having to put up council tax. "But they're not doing it because they want to. It is because the government has taken away 40% of their funding. "So we have actually instructed lawyers, as the Conservative Party, to see if we can challenge the government on this decision."Pressed on how the rise will still mean Wandsworth's council tax is lower than many councils across the country, Badenoch said it would still worry some families."I think if you suddenly have a nearly 100% increase in your council tax, you would be extremely worried. Families have budgets," she said."Just because on average it's lower than somewhere else doesn't mean that people are going to be able to afford it."She refused to say what alternative rate of increase she would propose, but questioned why a 40% cut was being imposed on the council when "Andy Burnham has not found 40% of anything to cut" himself.She also defended her record as local government minister when the Tories were in Downing Street, despite Conservative governments having slashed some council grants.Wandsworth Council's Tory deputy leader said on Tuesday: "Higher council tax will not be easy or welcome. We do not regard it as fair and will continue to challenge the government by every possible means."Other London councils including Westminster, Richmond and Kensington and Chelsea along with Wandsworth are consulting on plans to use the Sustainable Communities Act to challenge government funding cuts.As a result of the central government cuts, the usual cap of 5% annual council tax rises was lifted for all these councils as well as Windsor and Maidenhead in Berkshire.Leader of the opposition in Wandsworth, Labour councillor Simon Hogg, said: "It's outrageous, it is stunning. People who don't know how to run the council panicking and making you pay the price."This increase is unfair, it's unnecessary and we oppose it."However, the PoliticsHome website reported, external that three Labour MPs in Wandsworth - Rosena Allin-Khan, Fleur Anderson and Marsha de Cordova - have refused to back the council's appeal to the government to stop the funding cuts.The three Labour MPs claimed the council "was in a strong financial position" before the Tories took over at the May elections earlier this year.A spokesperson for the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government said: "Local authorities decide the level of council tax they wish to set, but we are clear that in doing so they should put taxpayers first."We've made over £78bn available for council finances next year, with the majority of money unringfenced so local leaders can decide how best to spend on their local priorities."And we're fixing an outdated funding system so funding goes where need is greatest, while protecting councils through the transition and ensuring no area faces a cliff edge."

schema.headline: Badenoch brings in lawyers after 94% Wandsworth Council tax hike

title: MI5 accepts it gave evidence based on lies in neo-Nazi spy case
description: He said "MI5 accepts without reservation" the findings of a damning report which concluded that it gave evidence based on "lies" about having kept to
body: He said "MI5 accepts without reservation" the findings of a damning report which concluded that it gave evidence based on "lies" about having kept to its core secrecy policy - known as 'neither confirm nor deny' (NCND) - about the agent status of the neo-Nazi informant.The security service claimed it had maintained NCND and, consequently, the courts allowed it to keep information secret from a woman who was abused by him.But what MI5 said was untrue. The security service had in fact disclosed the man's agent status in phone calls to me, as it tried to persuade me not to investigate him in 2020.A panel of three senior judges - England and Wales' most senior judge, Lady Chief Justice Baroness Sue Carr, President of the King's Bench Division Dame Victoria Sharp and Mr Justice Chamberlain - is considering what action to take over the false evidence.In particular, it will decide whether to initiate contempt of court proceedings against certain MI5 officers or MI5 itself. Any such move would be unprecedented.The report, by then-deputy investigatory powers commissioner Sir John Goldring, found that one senior MI5 spy - known as Officer 2 - lied repeatedly, while another - Officer 3 - misled his own colleagues and lied about what he was told. He also found there were "serious and systemic failures in MI5's conduct" throughout the case.Otty said MI5 "fully accepts and acknowledges the gravity of the issues raised" in the report, published in July, and they must never happen again.He added that MI5 had committed to a major programme of reform under the leadership of director general Sir Ken McCallum.Otty argued against contempt proceedings being brought, saying it would not be in the public interest given Sir John's detailed investigation, MI5's apologies, and its commitment to a programme of reform.He said Officer 2 had resigned from the service and that Officer 3 had been suspended and was facing disciplinary proceedings, which could lead to his dismissal.Lawyers for both officers also argued against launching contempt proceedings.Matthew Butt KC, for Officer 2, said said the officer accepted that his conduct had fallen "below the standard expected of him", for which he apologised and expressed regret. But he said he denied acting dishonestly or having interfered with the administration of justice, and did not accept the report's findings.Aaron Watkins apologised on behalf of Officer 3 and accepted his conduct "undoubtably" contributed to the courts and parties involved being misled, but denied it had been the result of dishonesty.He said the evidence presented by Sir John fell short of the threshold for contempt of court, and said such proceedings would not be in the public interest because there had already been a thorough investigation.Meanwhile, lawyers for the BBC said the corporation considered the threshold had been met and said there was a "very clear public interest" in doing so.Jude Bunting KC said providing false evidence was "a particularly serious affront to the administration of justice" and noted that while MI5 now offered a sincere apology to the court, its response when the lies were first exposed was "not consistent with transparency or responsibility".The case centres around the foreign neo-Nazi misogynist - an MI5 informant known as Agent X who used his security service role as a tool of abuse.He coercively controlled his partner, known by the alias Beth, and attacked her with a machete. MI5 then helped him go abroad to continue intelligence work while under police investigation.The government took the BBC to court in 2022 in a failed attempt to block its investigation into X, but won him legal anonymity. Beth then sued MI5 at the Investigatory Powers Tribunal, and in 2024 she sought a review of a ruling at the High Court.Arguing for secrecy in all three courts, the security service told judges that it had always stuck to its core secrecy policy and never told anyone whether X was an agent, including me. The courts were told this in a sworn statement from a senior officer, a deputy director called Witness A.The courts accepted MI5's arguments. This meant Beth and everyone else was banned from ever officially being told X was an agent and denied access to the key evidence. She was left at a serious disadvantage and may have lost the case.Officer 2 had tried to cover up for the man, falsely saying he was not an abusive misogynist nor a real extremist.Following the court decision in late 2024, I challenged MI5 and said they had lied to the courts. MI5 aggressively maintained its position that its NCND policy had been maintained until I produced evidence proving it was untrue, including a recording of one of the calls with Officer 2.Because of the BBC's revelations, two official inquiries took place which absolved MI5 and its officers of deliberate wrongdoing, claiming the false evidence was down to mistakes and poor memories.But, in July 2025, a panel of senior High Court judges ruled that the investigations carried out by MI5 suffered from "serious procedural deficiencies" and that "we cannot rely on their conclusions".Sir John's investigation was ordered by the prime minister in September 2025 after MI5's explanations about what happened were rejected as deficient and unreliable.Charlotte Kilroy KC, for Beth, said contempt proceedings should be brought against Officers 2 and 3, as well as the Director General of MI5 Sir Ken McCallum in his capacity as the person with corporate responsibility for the organisation.In written submissions, she said the false evidence "did not emanate from one individual, or a "bad apple'" and was "sustained and long-lasting".She added: "There have been repeated efforts to prevent the truth emerging. The reality of the dishonesty and false evidence that has taken place has only emerged because MI5 was faced with incontrovertible proof of its wrongdoing."She told the court that the "function" of the Goldring report was to allow it to consider whether to bring contempt proceedings, meaning the report was never meant to be the final word."Contempt proceedings are essential", she said.

schema.headline: MI5 accepts it gave evidence based on lies in neo-Nazi spy case

title: Resident Evil movie: Zach Cregger 'not prepared' for fan response
description: First launched in 1996 on the original Sony PlayStation by Japanese developer Capcom, Resident Evil was a sensation.Rather than casting players as sup
body: First launched in 1996 on the original Sony PlayStation by Japanese developer Capcom, Resident Evil was a sensation.Rather than casting players as super-powered characters, as was the case with most video games in the 90s, it forced them to survive with limited resources.Thanks to smart reinventions and remakes, the series has managed to stay relevant, selling a total of 213 million copies since its debut.Some of its characters are among the most well-known in video games, and there are whole communities dedicated to discussing the lore of their universe.Cregger's Resident Evil follows the story of Bryan, an original character played by Austin Abrams who worked with the director on Weapons.He's a courier who agrees to deliver a package to a hospital in Raccoon City - a key location from the games.As Bryan makes his way to the drop-off, it becomes apparent he is caught in the middle of some sort of viral outbreak, with the infected becoming monstrous creatures.When the first trailer appeared online, many users swamped comment sections to complain about what they'd seen.Where were the beloved characters? The familiar monsters? Cregger says he had little interest in simply retelling the story of the Resident Evil games, but that didn't seem to calm some fans."I think I was naive," he says."I think I was expecting people to be excited to see a Resident Evil movie that felt in the spirit of the games."What I was trying to do is make a movie that really honoured the experience of playing them."According to most reviews, Cregger has achieved what he set out to do.In its three-star review, NME , externalasked whether it was "the first great horror movie game adaptation"."For a large chunk of the film's runtime, the answer is a resounding yes," wrote reviewer Jordan Bassett, who said Bryan's encounters become repetitive as the film wears on.Doug Jamieson, of The Jam Report, external, awarded four stars and said Cregger "understands adaptation as translation rather than imitation".In an eight out of 10 review, Looper, external critic Alastair Ryder wrote: "Zach Cregger has done the best job I've seen of translating the experience of playing a video game and making it feel cinematic."The verdict from fans remains to be seen, but Resident Evil looks to be on track to have a successful opening weekend at the box office.It follows recent video game adaptations such as the Minecraft and Super Mario Bros films, which were poorly reviewed but hugely popular.This isn't the first adaptation of Resident Evil, which was brought to cinema screens in 2002 - the first of six films overseen by writer-director Paul WS Anderson.His wife, Milla Jovovich, starred in each one, and while they have grown a cult following they were never a hit with critics.A 2021 "reboot" heavily based on the games and a 2022 Netflix series also failed to impress.The live-action rights to Resident Evil are owned by German production company Constantin Film - a fact fans have blamed for the perceived low quality of previous adaptations.Reports online suggest the company's agreement with Capcom prevents Constantin from setting its films in the same timeline as the games. Cregger told Newsbeat he'd had no contact with the game developer while working on the film."Nobody from Capcom ever reached out to me, ever, in any way," he said.Constantin Film declined to comment, but BBC Newsbeat has been told there was co-ordination between the developer and the film's producers behind the scenes.Cregger says it's "probably" impossible to please everyone, but it was never his intention to recreate the game on-screen."If I had delivered a faithful retelling of one of the stories in the games, I feel like those people would probably be upset with me for that too," he says."Because I would have messed it up somehow, inevitably."So all I can do is just tell the story that I think is going to be the very best story."If somebody's going to have a problem that it doesn't do exactly what they had in their mind of what a Resident Evil movie is, I can't say anything to that."

schema.headline: Resident Evil movie: Zach Cregger 'not prepared' for fan response

title: Not just 'Nice Guy Eddie': Lib Dems eager for leader to show radical side at party conference
description: Discontent bubbles not far from the surface as the Liberal Democrats gather for their conference this weekend.Two years on from their best ever genera
body: Discontent bubbles not far from the surface as the Liberal Democrats gather for their conference this weekend.Two years on from their best ever general election result, conversations with those on the party's frontbench, its MPs, and backroom staff reveal a frustration at what many see as a failure to capitalise on that success.Polling by YouGov in the build up to the conference highlighted the Lib Dems "have seen no real growth in support since the last general election" and if anything have slipped back."We lack the ability to say something new or interesting," said one senior Lib Dem MP. "There is no energy, no excitement."A frontbencher said: "With the possible exception of our position on Trump, you could characterise most of our press lines as 'a Lib Dem spokesperson said, steady on now, gently does it'."Others describe the party's approach as "boring" and are spooked by the rise of the Green Party under Zack Polanski.The party's leadership are aware of the anger. They insist this conference will be a "gear shift".Daisy Cooper, the deputy leader, told me it would be "a gloves-off kind of conference"."You'll see a bit of fighting talk," she said.Some of the caution until now has been deliberate. The party's leadership met over the last few months and discussed whether to copy Polanski's punchy, social media-focused style but decided it wouldn't appeal to the well-heeled areas of southern England that form the Lib Dem heartlands. Those involved in that decision point to Polanski's recent struggles and feel vindicated.But at all levels of the party there is an acknowledgement they lag behind other parties on grabbing attention on social media, highlighted by Andy Burnham's "social first" approach.The party has only recently rolled out training for its MPs on making social videos, something senior figures despair at."When we have a success we're very good at getting a leaflet sent out to supporters straight away," one senior MP said. "But we don't do that for socials."Digital and social media will be a focus of at least 17 fringe events at conference, as the party tries to improve its online communications.But others worry that social media is just the medium and the problem is with the message.One MP raised the majority of voters (52% according to YouGov,) who view the party as "weak" in recent polling; and the tendency to say it's unclear what the party stands for (43% believing the party was weak, to 18% thinking it was strong)."We need to become bolder and more radical," a senior MP added. "We need to be angry on behalf of our constituents."Another Lib Dem MP said: "We are stuck fighting the guerilla politics of local campaigning. There is no broader articulation of what a vision for Liberal Britain is."Even those most loyal to Davey admit the party was struggling to offer a clear and coherent message. The Lib Dems' success at the last general election was, the party's own strategists believe, because voters wanted to remove the Conservatives and the Lib Dems benefitted from that anti-Tory sentiment."We haven't yet answered why people should vote for us rather than against the Tories," admitted one senior advisor.In public, Lib Dem MPs are often coy about the possibility of a coalition government with Labour after the election. In private, there are no such reservations. In an election many think could produce a hung parliament with no party in overall majority, the Lib Dem ambition is to be kingmakers to block a Reform government."If you're a serious political party you exist to be in government," the same senior adviser said.Lib Dem strategists are confident they can retain most of the 72 seats they won in 2024. Their sights now are on the 27 others where they came second, most of which were won by the Conservatives.There is a sizeable group of Lib Dem MPs, and members of its frontbench, who openly question whether their problem is not with the message, nor the strategy, but with Davey, the leader."I think he's holding us back," said one of the party's spokespeople who is planning a tilt at the leadership if a race is triggered."The atmosphere is ripe for a leadership challenge," another MP, talking of the frustrations in the party, said. "But we don't have a Wes Streeting," they added, referring to Labour's defence secretary whose challenge to Sir Keir Starmer undermined his leadership."There is a lack of an ambitious, young alternative putting themselves out there to show a different way."Davey's supporters in the party point to his experience of government and insist there is no one better to replace him. They also dismiss national polling as the way to measure the Lib Dem's standing."I'd like to be on more than 10% [in national opinion polls]," one frontbencher loyal to Davey said. "But I'd prefer to be on 10% and looking at winning 80 seats than on 15% and winning four.""You look at our ground game and you look at our local election results," another said, pointing to gains the party made at this year's May elections. "That shows you that our strategy is definitely working."But frustration bubbles away. And plenty in the party are looking at alternatives to Davey, like the party's President Josh Babarinde or Cooper, and question why they aren't setting out alternative visions.Both will give speeches at the conference, as will the home affairs spokesperson Max Wilkinson.So what of Cooper, who many consider the frontrunner to succeed Davey?"Ed is absolutely the right leader," she tells me. "I really like being deputy leader to Ed. We work together as a team. I think we complement each other."Would she want to be leader? "There is no vacancy," she says. Ever? "There is no vacancy at the moment," she replies.

schema.headline: Not just 'Nice Guy Eddie': Lib Dems eager for leader to show radical side at party conference

title: Spotted wildcat from Bolivian forest revealed as new species
description: Only one confirmed living member of the species is known - a cat in a rescue sanctuary in Bolivia - but scientists believe others exist.It was this 10
body: Only one confirmed living member of the species is known - a cat in a rescue sanctuary in Bolivia - but scientists believe others exist.It was this 10-year-old cat, nicknamed 'Tigrino', that set scientists on the path to discovery. Bolivian scientist Dr Nogales-Ascarrunz was volunteering at the sanctuary when she noticed the cat looked unusual.It had been found in the forest by a local resident, who initially thought it was a domestic kitten. As it grew older, however, it became clear that it did not behave like a house cat.Dr Nogales-Ascarrunz had heard of other sightings of small wild cats in the dense forests of the country's Yungas region, but these had not been investigated by scientists.To solve the mystery, she joined forces with other researchers from around the world to investigate the family history of tiger cats, using DNA from living animals and museum specimens."There's so few records or pictures, no individual in a museum, so it was hiding because nobody was looking," said Eduardo Eizirik, a conservation geneticist at the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio Grande do Sul in Brazil.The study, published in Current Biology, external, uncovered further surprises, suggesting there are five rather than three tiger cat species, including the newly described Tilcaya cat (Leopardus tilcayo) of Bolivia.

schema.headline: Spotted wildcat from Bolivian forest revealed as new species

title: Russian hybrid attacks against Europe intensifying, says Macron
description: Hybrid warfare or hybrid attacks are loose terms which tend to describe non-military methods, for example cyberattacks, sabotage or misinformation, de
body: Hybrid warfare or hybrid attacks are loose terms which tend to describe non-military methods, for example cyberattacks, sabotage or misinformation, designed to exert pressure and destabilise an adversary.These are quite often employed using proxies, but Russia always denies involvement in such attacks despite growing evidence to the contrary.The French president was speaking to journalists after meeting party leaders to discuss the security impact of the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine.Macron mentioned last month's drone attack on Leipzig airport in Germany, blamed on Russia, and remarks by Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk suggesting Russia was planning drone and missile strikes against Poland and other countries on Nato's eastern flank."In recent weeks, the Russian hybrid threat against Europeans and against France has intensified," he said."The intent is to intimidate us and break our effort to support Ukraine. The result will be the exact opposite. We are not intimidated because we know that our security today and tomorrow is at stake in Ukraine."On Thursday Tusk told Polish MPs that Russian plans included strikes by drones and missiles on countries supporting Ukraine. He said there was a "real risk" of such strikes on the territory of Nato countries, with Moscow then claiming that they were "accidental", in an attempt to split the alliance.Last Sunday, a Russian drone hit a passenger train near the Ukraine-Poland border shortly after former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson and top European security officials had passed through along the same line.Ukraine said all the passengers had been evacuated just minutes before the strike at Yahodyn, which hit the train's engine.There have also been a number of suspicious fires at defence facilities from Italy to Estonia, with some of the affected countries blaming Russia.Russian President Vladimir Putin has repeatedly said Russia does not plan to attack Europe, but Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov warned European nations against sending troops to Ukraine, which would be seen by Russia as a declaration of war."If Europe attacks Russia, it will be a completely different war, and it will be very short," he said.Meanwhile on Friday, Russia reiterated its warning to the UK that any British military facilities in Ukraine used to strike Russian territory were "legitimate targets". It reserved the right to take "necessary counter-measures" in response to the UK's "fiercely confrontational stance regarding Ukraine", referring to its supply of drones and other weapon systems to Kyiv.Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

schema.headline: Russian hybrid attacks against Europe intensifying, says Macron

title: England v Canada: Sophie de Goede still loses sleep over World Cup final loss
description: It is nearly a year since Canada lost the Women's Rugby World Cup final to England - but time has not been a healer for everyone."Four to five nights
body: It is nearly a year since Canada lost the Women's Rugby World Cup final to England - but time has not been a healer for everyone."Four to five nights a week I can't fall asleep because I'm still thinking about the final," says Canada captain Sophie de Goede, who is preparing to take on the world champions this Saturday at Sandy Park in Exeter.So, is this match revenge for the side ranked third in the world?Canada head coach Kevin Rouet is keen to play this down: "Revenge is a good brand but they [England] won the final of the World Cup - that was the most important game to win, the next important games will be in the World Cup 2029."After Canada, England play New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, before two more tests against Canada in Toronto and Ottawa. In recent history, England's women have never faced such tough successive opposition.Red Roses head coach John Mitchell says the games are an "audition" for the 2029 World Cup."You look at the geography that we're going to cover, we're not always going to be in our training base. We're going to be going to different facilities. It's a challenge," he said."It's going to be really cool to see how they handle pressure as well. I think the Red Roses are very good around pressure because I think it reveals how much they care".There continues to be misconceptions around the status of the Canadian women: they are professional athletes but contracts, as with most other nations, do not yet compare to England's women.The Canadian programme involves a clever strategy of using England's domestic PWR league to develop its players.There are 25 Canadians in PWR and the current Canada coaching staff includes Kevin Rouet and Alex Austerberry, who both coach Saracens Women, and Nathan Smith from Loughborough Lightning."It's not like we're coming in to spy," joked De Goede. "We just don't have the quality league [in Canada]."Canada are not the only country to do this - PWR is littered with top internationals from across the globe.Mitchell has told BBC Sport that he and Charlie Hayter, head of women's performance at England Rugby, have lobbied to increase PWR game time for English Qualified Players (EQP) from next season.Mitchell has frequently pushed his theory that players who can reach 1,000 PWR playing minutes a season "gives them a higher probability" of playing for the Red Roses."I haven't enjoyed seeing young English players between 21 and 23 not getting enough minutes," he said."I think that number [1,000] is very meaningful."The RFU confirmed to BBC Sport the current requirements around 13 EQP players on average across matchday squads will remain. However, the lure of signing foreign talent will be dampened by the removal of club injury credit, which helps cover the cost of replacing an injured player.From the 2027-28 season, only players who sustain an injury while on international duty for one of England's representative teams will be eligible.Besides this, if any EQP player is captured by another union, they will only be able to hold their EQP status until the end of that season.

schema.headline: England v Canada: Sophie de Goede still loses sleep over World Cup final loss

title: Flight chaos caused by millisecond software defect, says air traffic control body
description: An air traffic control failure that sparked widespread travel chaos earlier this month was caused by a "software defect" affecting the system underpin
body: An air traffic control failure that sparked widespread travel chaos earlier this month was caused by a "software defect" affecting the system underpinning UK air space management, the national air traffic service Nats has said.The problem happened "in the space of a millisecond", Nats said, leading to the system producing corrupted data.The failure led to more than 2,000 flights being cancelled and hundreds of thousands of passengers affected, with some sleeping on airport floors or getting stuck overseas.Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander called the disruption "completely unacceptable", while industry body Airlines UK is writing to Nats to demand immediate compensation for costs incurred.The incident prompted questions over the resilience of Nats' systems, and some airlines questioned the position of its chief executive Martin Rolfe.There has also been anger from passengers about how much support they got from airlines, and about the fact that they are unlikely to be entitled to compensation because the regulator judges the situation was extraordinary circumstances.In an initial report, external, Nats said the software defect meant air traffic controllers had reduced information available, so restrictions were put in place to limit air traffic to maintain safety.The defect occurred at 10:00am on 8 September, but it did not become apparent this was a serious problem for another two and a half hours.The system restart did not start until just after 3:15pm, and restrictions on UK airspace were not lifted until 7:30pm.Flights in and out of the UK's main airports were affected, including Heathrow, Gatwick, Luton and Glasgow.The disruption took days to completely resolve because of the number of planes and crew left out of place.Martin Rolfe apologised to those affected by the disruption."It's our job to get people where they want to go, quickly and without delay and we are devastated when that goes wrong," he said."However, our primary role is to keep our skies safe, and everyone who flies through them. At no point last week was safety in question."Reacting to the Nats report, the transport secretary described the disruption as "completely unacceptable" and "frustrating" for passengers, airlines and airports."It's clear we need to urgently understand why this issue was not discovered and fixed before it caused chaos," Alexander said, adding that a Civil Aviation Authority review was underway.This is the third national air traffic incident in the past three years.In 2023, a computer shutdown over the August bank holiday weekend caused chaos for 700,000 passengers.There was another, smaller Nats outage in 2025, which caused 150 cancellations.Tim Alderslade, chief executive of Airlines UK, said: "Once again, it is passengers who have suffered and airlines who have picked up the pieces - and the tab - of an ATC [Air Traffic Control] system failure, while Nats itself faces no real consequences."He added that passengers deserved "commitment and proof that the system is being fixed".Alderslade also said Airlines UK was writing to NATS "to demand immediate compensation for the costs incurred and a credible plan to improve resilience."Addie Kitson, 26, had been on holiday in China when her flight home was diverted to Sweden."I thought I landed fine" she told the BBC, "but then they went: 'Welcome to Stockholm' and I went: 'Ooh, that's not London'".After being told about the issues affecting UK airspace, passengers were kept on the plane for a few hours, and then spent 19 hours inside Stockholm airport.Addie ended up with nearly £100 in unexpected costs after having to buy refreshments, adaptors and to pay for Wi-Fi to work."I got one £11 food voucher that didn't even cover the cost of a sandwich in Stockholm airport", Addie said.Addie questioned the rules around compensation, saying there had been multiple air traffic outages. "It doesn't seem that extraordinary," she said.

schema.headline: Flight chaos caused by millisecond software defect, says air traffic control body

title: Portugal: Cristiano Ronaldo named in new coach Jorge Jesus' first squad
description: Cristiano Ronaldo has been named in the first squad selected by new Portugal coach Jorge Jesus, ending speculation the 41-year-old could retire from i
body: Cristiano Ronaldo has been named in the first squad selected by new Portugal coach Jorge Jesus, ending speculation the 41-year-old could retire from international football.Ronaldo refused to confirm whether he would continue to play for his country after Portugal's World Cup round-of-16 defeat by eventual winners Spain in July.But the Al-Nassr forward is part of a 25-man group chosen for Portugal's four Nations League games between 24 September and 4 October.Jesus has replaced Roberto Martinez, who stepped down as Portugal coach after their World Cup exit.The 72-year-old was Ronaldo's club boss last season, when the pair helped Al-Nassr win the Saudi Pro League for the first time in seven years.The former Manchester United Real Madrid forward, who announced that this summer's World Cup would be his last, was in tears after Portugal's World Cup exit.When asked if he would keep playing for his country, he said: "I will meet the family and take decisions with a calm head."This sparked speculation he could follow his great rival Lionel Messi and retire from international football.Ronaldo will turn 42 before next summer's Nations League finals and will be 43 by Euro 2028.The oldest player in the history of the Euros is Ronaldo's former Portugal team-mate Pepe, who was 41 and 130 days for his last game at Euro 2024.Manchester United pair Diogo Dalot and Bruno Fernandes are also in the squad, along with Ruben Dias (Manchester City) and Pedro Neto (Chelsea).Portugal are at home to Wales on 24 September (19:45 BST) and away to Norway three days later. They then play in Denmark on 1 October and return home to host Norway on 4 October.

schema.headline: Portugal: Cristiano Ronaldo named in new coach Jorge Jesus' first squad

title: Police begin operation to move migrants from Ceuta beaches
description: Police have begun moving hundreds of migrants in Ceuta to a new tented site in the port area of the Spanish territory in north Africa.Officers struggl
body: Police have begun moving hundreds of migrants in Ceuta to a new tented site in the port area of the Spanish territory in north Africa.Officers struggled to contain crowds of people jostling to secure a place at the site after weeks of living on the beaches. Shots could be heard, with reports that police fired into the air.Several hundred migrants have now reached the camp, which has a capacity for 1,700 people.Most of the 72,000 migrants who breached the border from Morocco in July have returned. Ceuta's authorities have estimated that 13,000 remain in the enclave, but the Spanish central government has said it is lower.The operation began at about 07:00 local time (05:00 GMT) on Friday, with more than 3,000 migrants being transferred, according to the Spanish government-owned news agency Efe.During the process, some migrants broke through the cordon along the designated 2km (1.2 mile) route to the port. Video shows young men running in the darkness as police tried to maintain control.More than 170 police officers have been deployed, including drone technicians, Efe reported. It added that the situation was later "brought under control quickly", and the operation was able to continue.The operation is part of the government's attempt to concentrate the migrants in facilities where they can be identified and cared for while their administrative status is individually determined.The chaotic scenes will do little to dampen opposition criticism in Spain of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who has faced strong criticism over his handling of the crisis.Since the migrant influx, residents of the 18.5 sq km (7.2 sq miles) territory have expressed safety concerns. Some have destroyed shelters and blocked aid being supplied to the migrants.Ceuta's Mayor Juan Jesus Vivas told lawmakers in the European Parliament earlier this month that the migrants had turned Ceuta into a "pressure cooker"."The city is completely different than it was before this event, Ceutans have lost their joy and their lifestyles have been completely shaken up," the conservative mayor said.The opposition also accused Sánchez of knowing about the influx of migrants in advance. Sánchez has insisted that it was impossible to predict, but according to government documents, its intelligence services had warned of social media calls for a mass migrant crossing into Ceuta the day before the events happened.Ester Muñoz of the conservative People's Party said the government was "directly responsible for the invasion of Ceuta and for those who died".Sanchez has blamed trafficking gangs and has also said the crisis was sparked by hoaxes and rumours spread by social media.Ceuta was "a humanitarian crisis and also an administrative challenge within the city itself", the prime minister said.

schema.headline: Police begin operation to move migrants from Ceuta beaches

title: Oxford United apologises for United 93 shirt advert
description: A football club has apologised after it published images of a new clothing line with "United 93" printed on the back - the call sign of one of the air
body: A football club has apologised after it published images of a new clothing line with "United 93" printed on the back - the call sign of one of the aircraft hijacked on 9/11. The clothing was supposed to make reference to Oxford United's founding year of 1893. However, it said it had been released "without understanding of the historical context and associations". United Airlines Flight 93 crashed in Shanksville, Pennsylvania, killing all 44 people on board after being hijacked on 11 September 2001. A docudrama film titled United 93 was made about the tragedy and released in 2006. Oxford United was founded in 1893 as an amateur club called Headington and now plays in League One - the third tier of the English football pyramid. In a statement, the club said its Campus Clothing range had been withdrawn and it "sincerely apologised" for the error."It should not have reached the point of sale and we take full responsibility for not undertaking proper due diligence," it said. "We have removed the collection with immediate effect and are reviewing our approval processes to ensure nothing like this happens again."The 9/11 attacks saw 19 Al Qaeda members hijack four commercial passenger planes in the US.Two of them were flown into the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, resulting in them both collapsing.Another plane struck the Pentagon, near Washington DC, while the fourth plane - United 93 - crashed in rural Pennsylvania. It was believed to be destined for the US Capitol Building, also in Washington DC.The attacks killed 2,977 people and injured tens of thousands more.

schema.headline: Oxford United apologises for United 93 shirt advert

title: JJ Gabriel: Man Utd youngster travels to Barcelona amid speculation over future
description: Gabriel has not trained at United since scoring a hat-trick on his Uefa Youth League debut on 10 September. Tournament rules prevent him from playing
body: Gabriel has not trained at United since scoring a hat-trick on his Uefa Youth League debut on 10 September. Tournament rules prevent him from playing for a side other than United in this season's competition.Sources close to Gabriel were furious the club did not register him for their Champions League opener with Sabah FK, which Michael Carrick's side won 4-0.The United manager was again asked about Gabriel on Friday at his news conference to preview Sunday's Premier League match against Fulham."He's a young boy, JJ, and I think it's important we don't play anything out here," he said. "With the exposure and scrutiny and everything, you got to be careful and be sensible and think of him as much as anything."The situation will work itself out, whatever way it's going to work itself out. Making sure he's OK is the important thing."Gabriel scored in his first two Premier League 2 outings for United this season but will not be involved against Brentford at Leigh Sports Village on Friday.

schema.headline: JJ Gabriel: Man Utd youngster travels to Barcelona amid speculation over future

title: We bought our £242,000 home without a deposit - here's how
description: Image source, Conroy & AmberImage caption, The couple are aware of the risks that come with their no-deposit mortgageByDaniel ThomasBusiness reporterU
body: Image source, Conroy & AmberImage caption, The couple are aware of the risks that come with their no-deposit mortgageByDaniel ThomasBusiness reporterUpdated 4 hours agoUntil last year, Conroy, 32, and his partner Amber, 28, saw little prospect of owning their own home. They were renting in central Manchester where they work and could not afford to save up for a deposit. Then they came across a relatively niche, and some experts say riskier, type of mortgage that offered a solution. The Track Record mortgage from Skipton Building Society covers 100% of the value of a property, with the borrower paying nothing upfront. Borrowers must meet strict eligibility checks and pay a higher interest rate - in Conroy and Amber's case 5.33% fixed for five years - but they were happy to do this. And in August they bought a four-bed home for £242,000 in Swinton on the edge of Manchester."I don't think it's dawned on us it's really ours," says Conroy, a video editor. The return of low-deposit dealsAccording to the Bank of England, the share of UK mortgages with deposits worth less than 10% of the property's value is currently the highest it has been since 2008, external when such loans were widely available.The average deposit for first-time buyers is currently around 20%.It comes as lenders such as Lloyds, Santander, Skipton and Yorkshire Building Society have launched a raft of new mortgage deals over the last few years covering upwards of 95% of the value of a property, and in some cases as much as 100%.They say they want to help first-time buyers get on the housing ladder as property prices continue to rise and while saving for a deposit remains a struggle.But these loans tend to charge higher rates, aren't available for all types of property or borrower, and come with risks customers should be aware of.Image source, SuppliedImage caption, Conroy and Amber thought they would be renting for the foreseeable futureConroy and Amber, a solicitor, have a 25-year loan with monthly repayments of £1,500 - roughly what they were paying in rent. He says they feel comfortable with the higher cost because they "earn quite well" and expect their salaries to rise. But he is aware there is a greater risk of falling into negative equity with a no- or low-deposit mortgage. That is when the value of a property falls below the value of the loan still owed on it - leaving the borrower with potentially painful costs if they suddenly have to sell.Conroy says they plan to overpay their mortgage for the first five years to build up more equity in their home."There is always the element of a gamble with the property market," he says.  "But I have researched the area we moved to and don't think house prices are going to drop." 'We plan to stay here our whole lives'Twenty-seven-year-old Bronya and her partner George, 29, also used a low-deposit mortgage to buy their four-bedroom house in Rhuddlan, North Wales in August. Lloyds lent them £258,000 - roughly 98% of the property's value - over a 33-year term and they only had to put down £5,000 as a deposit.The couple pay an interest rate of 5.89%, fixed for five years, equating to monthly repayments of £1,400 - about the same as what they paid to rent a one-bed flat before.Image source, SuppliedImage caption, Bronya and George bought their first home this year with a roughly 2% depositBronya, a civil servant, says they could have put down a bigger deposit but wanted to use their savings for a renovation project costing upwards of £20,000.They are aware of the risks of negative equity but believe the refurbishment will boost the value of their home."We also plan to stay here our whole lives," George adds, explaining that they are prepared to ride out any dips in the property market.Image source, SuppliedImage caption, The couple are renovating their homeWidespread uptake of low-deposit mortgages by borrowers who could not afford them was seen as a major factor in the 2008 global financial crisis.But today's deals have much stronger affordability checks and do not pose the same risks, says David Hollingworth, associate director at brokers L&C Mortgages.Borrowers of Skipton's zero-deposit mortgage, for example, have to prove they have kept up with their rent for at least 12 consecutive months and credit payments for the last six months.And Lloyds won't issue one of its £5,000 deposit mortgages for new-build properties and shared ownership homes.Hollingworth says lenders are recognising that some people have "good affordability but may be struggling to save for a deposit while paying a rent and dealing with cost of living pressures".Following a recent rule change, he adds, lenders are also offering more "flex" on how much someone can borrow as long as it's within their means. Nevertheless, he urges borrowers to use common sense.  "Think carefully - what do monthly payments look like? Are you aware that interest rates could go up?"Get in touchAre you buying your first home? How have you managed it?

schema.headline: We bought our £242,000 home without a deposit - here's how

title: Afghan female medical students fear being sent home from Pakistan
description: Nooria, which is not her real name, still remembers one of the moments that made her want to be a doctor.It was back home in a village in Afghanistan,
body: Nooria, which is not her real name, still remembers one of the moments that made her want to be a doctor.It was back home in a village in Afghanistan, where she was born. A 13-year-old boy there became sick and died because of appendicitis."He was completely healthy, but the road was blocked and he died on the way. There are multiple incidents just like this.""That and the potential I saw in myself, I thought I can be a doctor for them, I can help."She fears that dream could now be over and that she could be sent back to Afghanistan. That would be the end of any chance at a career for Nooria who, as a woman, is barred from studying or working by Afghanistan's Taliban government.Earlier this month, Pakistan's Medical and Dental Council - the medical education regulator - issued a letter to all medical and dental colleges across the country saying that students from Afghanistan studying in their colleges must return to their home country. Failure to follow the directive, it said, would be "viewed seriously" and may lead to regulatory action. A temporary stay order from the Lahore High Court stopped students in Punjab, such as Nooria, from being deported immediately until the next hearing, scheduled for Friday. There is no certainty that the stay will continue.Since 2023, hundreds of thousands of Afghans have been deported from Pakistan and over two million have left according to the UN. These numbers increased as the relationship between Pakistan and Afghanistan dramatically deteriorated in the last year. Pakistan has accused Afghanistan's Taliban government of harbouring militant groups, which it denies.The announcement from the medical council was met with a strong reaction. Amnesty International called the decision "patently discriminatory and arbitrary" and said that "Pakistan has obligations under international human rights law to uphold the right to education without discrimination on the basis of national origin." Several of Pakistan's former envoys to Afghanistan also urged the council to reconsider; one called it "shocking" and "a question of humanity, compassion and Pakistan's own moral responsibility".The council told the BBC that they can give no further comment while the court case continues, but their lawyer has told the BBC that none of the Afghan students were registered with PMDC. The students say that this is the responsibility of their colleges, not them; a notification issued by the PMDC earlier this year, external directs colleges to ensure that students are registered.The medical and dental students the BBC has spoken to say they do not see how the relationship between the two countries should affect their ability to study.For Nooria, this stings even more because she says it took a lot for her to get here. She first began studying at Kabul University, but as the Taliban forces approached the city, she left. She was offered what she thought at the time was a lifeline: the opportunity to study medicine in Pakistan on a scholarship. Now a final year student at a medical university in Lahore, she says she has given everything to the course."I was studying, day and night. I couldn't sleep because there was so much pressure and knowledge that I had accumulated in my mind. I got used to it a bit, but I have compromised a lot. My relationships, talking to my family, spending time with my friends. I think I haven't lived for these years, I have only studied for my dream."So when she heard about the letter, Nooria was in shock. She's still nervous about the repercussions of speaking out, which is why she asked we don't reveal her name."We knocked on every door, our teachers, organisations, anyone we thought could help us. We are under so much pressure that we have completely forgotten about our studies, we don't know what will happen to us."Final year students like Nooria have their last exams in just a few months. Said Mubin, another final year student in Punjab, is in the same position."I was in complete despair, my mind was blank. It was like a panic situation because they were giving us very short time to evacuate the (accommodation), the college," he says.Other students have also brought cases across the country, but different directives have been issued, adding to the confusion. Some students told the BBC that they have finished their exams but not completed the practical training - known as a 'House Job' - to complete their medical education.Without completing their degrees, both Mubin, Nooria and many other medical and dental students the BBC spoke to, fear that none of their credits will be recognised by another institution."It means you have to start from zero, from your first year," Mubin says.Both Nooria and Mubin have valid student visas, seen by the BBC. The PMDC did not provide the BBC with the number of students they believe are affected, but Anayatullah Momand, a spokesperson for the Afghan medical students, has said that they estimate it's approximately 1,000 medical and dental students, 65% of whom have visa holders. Some are still waiting for a visa, but Momand said that 15% have had their visas cancelled or have not yet applied for one. While the medical council's letter makes no distinction between students with the right documents, Pakistan's Ministry for Foreign Affair's spokesman did. "Our policy is that those Afghan students who are in Pakistan on a valid visa and registered for a valid course will continue and complete his or her education," said Sajjad Haider Khan during a recorded press conference at the ministry.Similar comments were made the previous week, but the students say they have not seen any change to their situation.With the outcome of her studies still uncertain, Nooria has been trying not to think about what returning to Afghanistan could mean."My family counted on me. These five years I have sacrificed everything that would be zero, multiplied by zero. And then I would become a poor and helpless Afghan female, facing this destiny. I cannot imagine this."

schema.headline: Afghan female medical students fear being sent home from Pakistan
